title: Connecting the Dots: Mean, Median and Data

standard_text: Representative values of data: mean (average), median, mode and range; comparing data sets; reading bar graphs (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 Connecting the Dots worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 5): mean, median, mode, range, missing values and bar graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mean = sum ÷ count; median = middle value
key_sub: Put the data in order before finding the median.
body_html:
How it works

The mean (average) shares the total equally: add all the values and divide by how many there are.

The median is the middle value when the data are in order; with an even count, it is halfway between the two middle values. The mode is the most common value; the range is largest − smallest.

Example

Find the mean of 12, 15, 9, 20, 14.

Sum 70

70 ÷ 5

Answer: 14

Example

Find the median of 7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 2.

Order: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11

(5 + 7) ÷ 2

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

  • Finding the median without ordering the data.
  • Dividing by the wrong number of values.
  • Giving the largest value as the range.

faq.a: The sum of all values divided by the number of values.
The middle value when the data are arranged in order.

faq.q: When is the median better than the mean?
faq.a: When one or two values are very large or very small, because the median is not pulled by them.
